questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: How to open a restaurant
What it really means to be a foodie
Why fast food is unhealthy
The best cookery programmes on TV
questions.why: Neil says 'Today we're talking about being a foodie', and chef Angela Hartnett gives her view.

questions.q: How does Rob describe a foodie?
options: Someone who eats out every night
Someone who works as a chef in a restaurant or a hotel kitchen
Someone very interested in preparing and eating good food
Someone who loves fast food
questions.why: Rob says a foodie has a strong interest in food, likes preparing and eating it and using good ingredients.

questions.q: According to Angela Hartnett, what do people who call themselves foodies usually do?
options: Buy cookbooks and watch TV, but cook only a little
Cook a big meal every day for all of their families
Grow their own vegetables
Work in restaurants
questions.why: She says they 'buy the books, watch TV and will cook a little bit'.

questions.q: What is Angela Hartnett's idea of a true foodie?
options: Someone who eats in expensive restaurants
Someone who writes cookery books and presents shows on television
Someone who only buys organic food
Someone who shops daily and knows the parts of an animal
questions.why: She describes people who shop every day and 'understand one end of a pig from another'.

questions.q: Why does Hartnett mention her mother and grandmother?
options: They were famous chefs
They are examples of people who really knew about food
They taught her to cook in their own family restaurants
They didn't like cooking
questions.why: She says they made food and knew about what was expensive and about quality.

questions.q: What does Hartnett admit about her idea of a foodie?
options: It might be a bit idealistic
It is completely wrong
It is only true in Britain
It is too modern
questions.why: She says 'maybe that's a bit romantic', meaning an imagined ideal.

questions.q: What is Hartnett's opinion of food in Britain?
options: It is cheap and good quality
It is much better than in the rest of Europe
It is too expensive for lots of people
It is too unhealthy
questions.why: She says food is expensive and 'I don't think it's affordable for lots of people'.

questions.q: What is Hartnett worried might happen?
options: Restaurants might close
People might stop watching cookery shows and buying cookbooks
People might eat too much
People might forget how to cook a cheap family meal
questions.why: She worries we'll stop knowing how to make a meal for a family of four for five pounds.
